chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'From where does the distinction lie between the Mutamatti' and the Mu'tamir?' He said: 'The Mutamatti' is bound to the Hajj, and the Mu'tamir, when he is free from it, goes wherever he wishes. And Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) performed Umra in Dhi al-Hijjah, then he departed on the Day of Tarwiyah to Iraq, while the people were departing to Mina. And there is no harm in performing Umra in Dhi al-Hijjah for one who does not intend Hajj.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The Mutamatti', one who performs Umra and remains in the state of Ihram until Hajj rites are completed.
key_terms.الْمُعْتَمِرُ: The Mu'tamir, one who performs Umra and exits the state of Ihram, free to travel.
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhi al-Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, during which Hajj is performed.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a valley and campsite near Mecca where pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq.
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah, the 8th of Dhi al-Hijjah.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a Mutamatti' and a Mu'tamir in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the ritual status of the Mutamatti' versus the Mu'tamir, emphasizing that the former remains in a state of Hajj connection while the latter is free to depart after Umra. It cites the precedent of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) performing Umra in Dhu al-Hijjah and traveling to Iraq on the Day of Tarwiyah, thereby validating Umra during the Hajj months for those not performing Hajj. This establishes a practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing and independence of Umra rituals.
